newsitem.title: USA: Trade, tourism seen fuelling Southeast US in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Trade, tourism seen fuelling Southeast US in 1997.

text.p: Tourism, international trade and commercial construction will drive the Southeast U.S. economy to outperform the rest of the nation in 1997, bank economists predicted Monday.
Consumer spending was is expected to slow below 1996 levels as credit card users become increasingly wary of added debt.
But First Union Corp still projects GDP growth of 3.1 percent for the Southeast region, compared with 2 perent nationally for 1997.
The Southeast's strongest gains will continuing to come from Florida, Georgia, Tennesee and the Carolinas, First Union economist and vice president Mark Vitner said.
Virginia and Maryland, harder hit by federal and military cuts, are gaining momentum but their performance will rise more in line with the rest of the country, he said.

Economists expect unemployment to remain low, with some sectors experiencing worker shortages. Already in Florida, corporate growth has been stalled by a dearth of entry-level service workers and highly skilled computer programmers.
